A **strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group** on the complex Hilbert
space $H$ is a map $U:\mathbb R\to\mathcal B(H)$ such that
$U(0)=I$, $U(s+t)=U(s)U(t)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$, each $U(t)$ is unitary
(that is, onto and norm preserving, equivalently $U(t)^*U(t)=U(t)U(t)^*=I$,
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), and the orbit maps
$t\mapsto U(t)x$ are continuous at every $t$ for every $x\in H$, from the
usual metric on $\mathbb R$ to the norm metric of $H$
([[def-metric-continuity]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with
spectral projection valued measure $E$, and set
$U(t):=e^{itT}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{it\lambda}\,dE(\lambda)$ for $t\in\mathbb R$.
Then $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group,
$U(t)D(T)=D(T)$ and $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$, and the derivative
$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(U(t)x-x)$ exists exactly for $x\in D(T)$, where it equals
$iTx$. Thus the generator of $U$ is $G=iT$, with $D(G)=D(T)$.

Its
**infinitesimal generator** is the linear operator $G$ with domain
$$D(G):=\Bigl\{x\in H:\ \lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(U(t)x-x\bigr)\ \text{exists in }H\Bigr\},\qquad Gx:=\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(U(t)x-x\bigr),$$
where this is the two-sided norm limit over real $t\ne0$: it has value $y$
precisely when for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that
$$0<|t|<\delta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \left\|\frac{U(t)x-x}{t}-y\right\|<\varepsilon.$$
Equivalently, defining the quotient's value at $t=0$ to be $y$ makes it
continuous there from the usual metric on $\mathbb R$ to the norm metric on
$H$ ([[def-metric-continuity]]). Such a $y$ is unique by the triangle
inequality.

1. there is a unique operator $\Phi_E(f)\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
   $$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,y\rangle=\int f\,dE_{x,y}\qquad(x,y\in H),$$
   and for every sequence $(s_n)$ of complex simple functions with
   $\|f-s_n\|_\infty\to0$ one has $\|\Phi_E(f)-\int s_n\,dE\|\to0$: the integral
   is obtained from uniform simple approximations and is independent of the
   approximating sequence;
2. $\|\Phi_E(f)\|\le\|f\|_\infty$, and for every $x\in H$
$$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,x\rangle=\int f\,dE_x,\qquad \|\Phi_E(f)x\|^2=\int|f|^2\,dE_x ;$$

$$D(f(E)):=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_X|f|^2\,dE_x<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,$$
where the scalar measures $E_x$ are those of
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]], and for $x\in D(f(E))$ set
$$f(E)x:=\lim_{n\to\infty}\Phi_E\bigl(f\,\mathbf 1_{\{|f|\le n\}}\bigr)x,$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

derivations.claim: Clause (a) is exactly the statement of the cited generation lemma, read in the notation $U(t)=e^{itT}$: it gives the group law, unitarity, $U(t)^{*}=U(-t)$, the invariance $U(t)D(T)=D(T)$, the commutation $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$, and the characterization of the difference quotient with limit $iTx$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]). [given, F1]

For bounded Borel $h$ and fixed $t$, [F2] and [F3] give $h(T)U(t)=\Phi_E(h)\Phi_E(f_t)=\Phi_E(hf_t)$, and multiplication of complex functions is commutative, so $\Phi_E(hf_t)=\Phi_E(f_th)=\Phi_E(f_t)\Phi_E(h)=U(t)h(T)$; this is the first assertion of (b). [given, F2, F3, algebra]

Let $x\in D(T)$. At $t=0$ the difference quotient converges to $iTx$ by [F1]. For fixed $t$ and $s\to0$ the group law gives $U(t+s)x-U(t)x=U(t)\bigl(U(s)x-x\bigr)$, hence $\frac1s\bigl(U(t+s)x-U(t)x\bigr)=U(t)\frac1s\bigl(U(s)x-x\bigr)\to U(t)iTx=iU(t)Tx$, because $U(t)$ is bounded and the limit in the last factor exists; the identity $iU(t)Tx=iTU(t)x$ is the commutation in [F1]. The derivative $t\mapsto iU(t)Tx$ is continuous because $U$ is strongly continuous and $U(t)Tx$ depends continuously on $t$; hence $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable at every $t$ with the displayed derivative. [given, F1, algebra]

Let $x\in H\setminus D(T)$ and suppose that $t\mapsto U(t)x$ were differentiable at some $t_0$ with derivative $y$. Then for $s\to0$, using the group law and boundedness of $U(-t_0)$, $\frac1s\bigl(U(s)x-x\bigr)=U(-t_0)\frac1s\bigl(U(t_0+s)x-U(t_0)x\bigr)\to U(-t_0)y$, so the difference quotient at $0$ would converge, contradicting [F1], which says that it converges exactly for $x\in D(T)$. Hence $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable at no point of $\mathbb R$. [given, F1, algebra]
Taking $h=\mathbf 1_B$ for a Borel set $B$ in step 1.2 and using $E(B)=\Phi_E(\mathbf 1_B)$ from [F3] gives $E(B)U(t)=U(t)E(B)$, the second assertion of (b). [step 1.2, F3]
Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 1.3 and 1.4 establish clauses (a), (b) and (c). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 1.4] ∎

derivations.claim: [Boundedness, norm and adjoint] $A(t)=U(-t)AU(t)$ is a product of bounded operators, so bounded, and $A(0)=A$; by [F2], $\|A(t)\|=\|A\|$ and $A(t)^{*}=U(t)^{*}A^{*}U(-t)^{*}=U(-t)A^{*}U(t)=A^{*}(t)$; hence $A$ self-adjoint implies $A(t)$ self-adjoint. For the covariance, $A(t+s)=U(-t-s)AU(t+s)=U(s)^{*}U(-t)AU(t)U(s)=U(s)^{*}A(t)U(s)$ by the group law. This is (a). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

[Time-invariance of the product-domain hypothesis] Assume $A\,D(T)\subseteq D(T)$. For $y\in D(T)$ one has $U(t)y\in D(T)$ by [F1], then $AU(t)y\in D(T)$ by hypothesis, and finally $U(-t)AU(t)y\in D(T)$ by [F1] again; thus $A(t)y=U(-t)AU(t)y\in D(T)$. [given, F1]

[Conjugation of the spectral measure] Assume $A$ self-adjoint with spectral PVM $E_A$. Fix $t$ and put $E'(B):=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$. Then $E'$ is a PVM: each $E'(B)$ is an orthogonal projection because $U(-t)=U(t)^{*}$ is unitary and $E_A(B)$ is an orthogonal projection; $E'(\varnothing)=0$, $E'(\mathbb R)=I$; and for pairwise disjoint Borel $B_n$ with union $B$, the strong countable additivity of $E_A$ gives $\sum_nE'(B_n)x=U(-t)\bigl(\sum_nE_A(B_n)U(t)x\bigr)\to U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)x=E'(B)x$ because $U(-t)$ is bounded. It is regular because its scalar measure in $x$ is $E'_x(B)=\|E'(B)x\|^{2}=\langle U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)x,x\rangle=\langle E_A(B)U(t)x,U(t)x\rangle=E_{A,U(t)x}(B)$, a regular Borel measure. [given, F1, F3, F4]

[Strong continuity] For $x\in H$, $A(t)x-A(s)x=U(-t)A\bigl(U(t)-U(s)\bigr)x+\bigl(U(-t)-U(-s)\bigr)AU(s)x$, and both terms tend to $0$ as $t\to s$ because $U$ is strongly continuous and $A$ is bounded; the norm bound is step 1.1. This is (c). [given, step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

[Equation of motion] Assume $A\,D(T)\subseteq D(T)$ and let $x\in D(T)$. Decompose $A(t+s)x-A(t)x=U(-t-s)A(U(t+s)x-U(t)x)+(U(-t-s)-U(-t))AU(t)x$; the first term divided by $s$ equals $U(-t-s)A\frac1s(U(t+s)x-U(t)x)$, and $\frac1s(U(t+s)x-U(t)x)\to iU(t)Tx$ by [F1], so it tends to $iU(-t)AU(t)Tx=iA(t)Tx$. For the second term, $y:=AU(t)x$ lies in $D(T)$ by step 1.2, and $\frac1s(U(-s)y-y)\to-iTy$ by [F1] applied at $0$ to the group $s\mapsto U(-s)$; hence the second term divided by $s$ equals $U(-t)\frac1s(U(-s)y-y)\to-iU(-t)Ty=-iTU(-t)y=-iTA(t)x$, using the commutation $TU(-t)=U(-t)T$ on $D(T)$ from [F1]. Adding the two limits gives $\frac{d}{dt}A(t)x=iA(t)Tx-iTA(t)x=-i(TA(t)-A(t)T)x$. This is (b). [given, step 1.2, F1, algebra]

[Identification as the spectral measure of $A(t)$] With $E'$ as in step 1.3, [F3] gives $\Phi_{E'}(g)=U(-t)\Phi_{E_A}(g)U(t)$ for bounded Borel $g$: the identity holds for indicators by definition of $E'$, extends to simple functions by linearity, and passes to uniform limits by the norm estimate of [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] clause 1. Applying the truncation definition [F4] with $g_n(\lambda)=\lambda\mathbf 1_{\{|\lambda|\le n\}}$ and $x\in H$ (the domain is all of $H$ because $A$ is bounded) gives $\int\lambda\,dE'(\lambda)x=\lim_n\Phi_{E'}(g_n)x=\lim_nU(-t)\Phi_{E_A}(g_n)U(t)x=U(-t)(\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda))U(t)x=U(-t)AU(t)x=A(t)x$, where the middle limit is interchanged with the bounded operator $U(-t)$ and $\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)=A$ is the spectral representation of the bounded self-adjoint $A$. Hence $E'$ represents the bounded self-adjoint $A(t)$, and by uniqueness [F4] it is the spectral PVM of $A(t)$. [given, step 1.3, F3, F4, algebra]

[Spectra] For a self-adjoint operator with spectral PVM $F$, the spectrum consists of the points $\lambda$ with $F((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))\ne0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ ([[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]] clause 4 with $f$ the identity). By step 2.3, $E_{A(t)}((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))=U(-t)E_A((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))U(t)$ is nonzero exactly when $E_A((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))$ is; hence $\sigma(A(t))=\sigma(A)$. [given, step 2.3, F4]
Steps 1.1, 2.1, 1.2, 2.2, 1.3, 2.3 and 3.1 prove (a)-(d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 2.2, step 1.3, step 2.3, step 3.1] ∎

derivations.claim: [Eigenrays are stationary] Assume (ii): $T\psi=\lambda\psi$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and set $u:=\psi/\|\psi\|$, so that $Tu=\lambda u$ and $\|u\|=1$. By [F3], $\int(\lambda'-\lambda)^{2}\,dE_u(\lambda')=\|(T-\lambda)u\|^{2}=0$; the integrand is nonnegative and measurable, so by [F4] it vanishes $E_u$-almost everywhere, that is, $E_u(\mathbb R\setminus\{\lambda\})=0$. Fix $t$ and put $g_t(\lambda'):=e^{it\lambda'}-e^{it\lambda}$, a bounded Borel function vanishing $E_u$-almost everywhere; by [F2], $\|U(t)u-e^{it\lambda}u\|^{2}=\|\Phi_E(g_t)u\|^{2}=\int|g_t|^{2}\,dE_u=0$, so $U(t)u=e^{it\lambda}u$ and, multiplying by $\|\psi\|$, $U(t)\psi=e^{it\lambda}\psi$. In particular $U(t)\psi$ is a multiple of $\psi$ for every $t$, which is (i). The reality of $\lambda$ is [F6] applied to the unit vector $u$. [given, F2, F3, F4, F6, algebra]

[The invariant span] Assume (i). Multiplication by the nonzero scalar $\|\psi\|^{-1}$ shows that $u:=\psi/\|\psi\|$ satisfies $U(t)u=c(t)u$ with $c(t)\in\mathbb C$ for every $t$; since $U(t)$ is unitary and $\|u\|=1$, one has $|c(t)|=1$. By [F5], $K:=\mathbb Cu$ is a closed subspace of $H$ and, with the restricted inner product, a complex Hilbert space; by (i) each $U(t)$ maps $K$ into $K$, and because $U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ also maps $K$ into $K$, the restriction $W(t):=U(t)|_K$ is a bijection of $K$ onto itself. [given, F1, F5, algebra]

[The restricted group] The maps $W(t)$ are unitary on $K$: they are norm preserving on $K$ because $U(t)$ is, and they are onto $K$ by step 1.2. The group law $W(t+s)=W(t)W(s)$ and the continuity of $t\mapsto W(t)x$ for each $x\in K$ are inherited from $U$. (a) **Energy law and moments.** For every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)E_H(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)E_H(B)\bigr)=\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ likewise $\|E_H(B)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|E_H(B)\psi\|^{2}$. If $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, the mean and the second moment of the energy law of $[\psi(0)]$ are finite and time-independent, with time-zero values $\langle H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0),\psi(0)\rangle$ and $\|H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0)\|^{2}$; if one of these moments is infinite at time zero, no equality of finite quantities is claimed.

(b) **Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be a bounded assigned sharp observable that is compatible with the energy ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (f)). Then its outcome law is time-independent: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B).$$

(a) **Unitary flow.** $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]) with $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$ and $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$; every orbit has constant norm, $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(0)\|$, so for $\psi(0)\ne0$ the ray $[\psi(t)]$ is a pure preparation of the model for every $t$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

(b) **Domain invariance.** $U(t)D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ for every $t$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)=U(t)H_{\mathrm{op}}$ on $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$: the flow preserves the energy domain and commutes with the energy there.

(c) **Schroedinger equation on the domain.** For $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ is norm-differentiable at every $t\in\mathbb R$, it stays in $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, and
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)\psi(0);$$
for $\psi(0)\in H\setminus D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve is norm-differentiable at no $t\in\mathbb R$, so the equation is not asserted there, although the evolution $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ remains continuous.

(d) **Density-operator evolution.** For every preparation $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and every $t$ the operator $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ is again a preparation: self-adjoint, positive, trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Moreover for every bounded operator $B$ the identity $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)B\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)U(t)^{*}BU(t)\bigr)$ holds.

(a) If a bounded operator $B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ satisfies

(a') If a bounded self-adjoint operator $S$ satisfies $SK\subseteq KS$ — that
is $S(Kx)=K(Sx)$ for every $x\in D(K)$ — then $SU(t)=U(t)S$ for every $t$.

(b) Let $F$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space
$(Y,\Sigma)$ with $F(S)E(C)=E(C)F(S)$ for all $S\in\Sigma$ and all Borel
$C\subseteq\mathbb R$. Then:

(i) $F(S)U(t)=U(t)F(S)$ for all $t$ and $S$;

(ii) for every density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H$ — a self-adjoint
positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$
([[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)) —
the numbers $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F(S))$ are independent of $t$:
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(U(t)\rho U(t)^*F(S)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F(S)\bigr) \qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ S\in\Sigma);$$

(c) applying (b) with $F=E$: for every density operator $\rho$ the energy law

the law $\|E(C)U(t)\psi\|^2=\|E(C)\psi\|^2$ is independent of $t$, and if
$\psi\in D(K)$ then both existing scalar moments are conserved:
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^k\,dE_{K,U(t)\psi}(\lambda) =\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^k\,dE_{K,\psi}(\lambda),\qquad k=1,2,$$
with the integrals finite at $t=0$ and equal to $\langle K\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $\|K\psi\|^2$ respectively; moments that are infinite at $t=0$ remain
outside the assertion;

(d) if $K\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and unit
$\psi\in D(K)$, then $U(t)\psi=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi$ for every $t$, and

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**Rays.** For $\psi\in H^{\times}$ the **ray** of $\psi$ is
$$[\psi]:=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C,\ z\ne0\}\subseteq H^{\times}.$$
A **ray** of $H$ is a subset of the form $[\psi]$ for some nonzero $\psi$, and an element of a ray is called a **representative** of it. The set of rays
$$R(H):=\{[\psi]:\psi\in H^{\times}\}$$
is the **ray space** of $H$. Two nonzero vectors $\psi,\varphi$ are **ray-equivalent** when they lie in a common ray, that is, when $\varphi=z\psi$ for some nonzero complex number $z$. Ray equivalence is an equivalence relation on $H^{\times}$: it is reflexive with $z=1$, symmetric with $z^{-1}$, and transitive by multiplying scalars. Its classes are exactly the rays, so $R(H)$ is the quotient set of $H^{\times}$ by this relation, and every nonzero vector lies in exactly one ray.
For every real $\theta$, $\exp(i\theta)=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$.
For all $z,w\in\mathbb C$, $\exp(z+w)=\exp z\exp w$. For real $x$, the complex value $\exp(x+0i)$ equals the published real exponential $e^x$.
